clue.text: Dancer gets label sprinkled with rain

indicators.note: sprinkling scatters things about, so the letters of these words are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancer has a label sprayed with rainwater, perhaps a soggy name tag at an outdoor show.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LABEL and RAIN together rearrange to BALLERINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet performer, a specific kind of dancer.

clue.text: Indian drug makes bishop droop

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to droop is to hang down limply

explanation.surface: A churchman wilts after taking some narcotic from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhang is a preparation of cannabis leaves traditionally drunk or eaten in India.

clue.text: I'm sluggish when chopping up the garlic

definitions.note: a first-person statement; the answer is the adjective describing the speaker

indicators.note: chopping something up breaks it into pieces that can be rearranged, so the letters get reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A cook complains of feeling drowsy while preparing garlic in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means lacking energy, slow and drowsy, exactly how a sluggish person feels.

clue.text: User-friendly drive means financial security

blocks.note: something user-friendly is easy to use
Drive is a common word in road names, so a drive is a kind of street

explanation.surface: Sounds like an advert claiming a simple-to-use car or computer drive brings money worries to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'User-friendly drive' reads like computing jargon, but the two words are clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on easy street is an idiom for living in comfort without money worries.

clue.text: I fall about, getting myself into disrepute

indicators.note: about suggests turning around and moving letters round into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
the speaker referring to themselves

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles around and so lands themselves in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a container signal, but here it only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill fame is an old term for a bad reputation, as in a house of ill fame, so it equals disrepute.

clue.text: Rambling answer: I'm getting smaller

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for answer
taken as written, without the apostrophe
less means smaller in amount

explanation.surface: A rambler replies that they are shrinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling talk or wandering has no direction or purpose, which is what aimless describes.

clue.text: Save about a pound for Labour

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A political plea to put aside money for the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes 'Labour' look like the British political party; it is the plain verb for toiling.
explanation.definitionFit: To slave is to work very hard like a servant, so it is a synonym of the verb labour.

clue.text: Two standing orders, nothing to write home about

blocks.note: SO is the abbreviation for standing order, taken twice

explanation.surface: A bank statement showing a couple of regular payments is pretty dull.
explanation.walkthrough: A standing order is a regular payment instruction to a British bank; SO abbreviates it.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means mediocre, and 'nothing to write home about' is an idiom for unremarkable.

clue.text: Mangle with top removed in the corner

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and removing it drops that letter

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old wringer stands in the corner of the laundry, its top off.
explanation.walkthrough: A mangle is an old-fashioned machine with rollers for wringing out washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner is the point where two lines or walls meet, which forms an angle.

clue.text: Joining up and settling rent with lemon!

indicators.note: settling suggests things shifting into a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new member signs up and pays the rent with a lemon, a comically useless currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is the act of registering or signing on, as when one joins up to a course or army.

clue.text: Voices detected in the musical "Tosca"

indicators.note: something detected inside has been found sitting within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Singing is heard in a performance of Puccini's opera Tosca.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosca is an opera, not a musical; the word is there only to supply its last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Altos are low female or high male singing voices, a part in a choir.

clue.text: Dullard returning newspaper to us is sweet

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the words that follow are read from end to start

blocks.note: a lump is a heavy, stupid person
a rag is a slang term for a low-quality newspaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool bringing the paper back to us turns out to be kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' seems to mean nice or kind, but it is a noun here for something sugary.
explanation.definitionFit: Lump sugar comes in small cubes and is a sweetener, here treated as something sweet.

clue.text: Is "The Mirror" two times smoother?

blocks.note: a mirror is a looking-glass
read the name a second time as the British tabloid newspaper, the Mirror

explanation.surface: A question of whether a tabloid's tone is twice as polished as before.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is used twice: once as a looking-glass and once as the newspaper of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasspaper is an abrasive sheet used to sand wood, so it is a tool for making surfaces even.

clue.text: Healthy in the spring

blocks.note: first meaning: in good health
second meaning: a source of water from the ground

explanation.surface: Feeling fit in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' seems to be the season, but it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for being in good health and a noun for a hole or source yielding water.

clue.text: Lady-love, lifting up clothes left and right, in the grip of Satan

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up raises the bottom letters to the top, so the word reads upwards
something in the grip of another is held inside it

blocks.note: rig is informal for an outfit of clothes
L is the abbreviation for left
the Fiend is a name for the Devil
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sweetheart hitches up her clothing to both sides, while held by the Devil.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the right goes in the grip of Satan; the left stays outside, after the turned clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady-love is an old-fashioned term for a man's beloved, a woman he is courting.

clue.text: Dirk to be keeping back dragon without tail

definitions.note: the actor's first name stands for his surname

indicators.note: a creature without its tail has lost its end, so the final letter goes
back means going in the opposite direction, so the letters run right to left
keeping means holding something within, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dagger is to restrain a tailless dragon, like a knight's quest.
explanation.walkthrough: A dirk is also a Scottish dagger, which is the picture the surface paints.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirk Bogarde was a British film actor, so his first name points to his surname.

clue.text: Knave of clubs or spades used in card-game

blocks.note: first meaning: a jack in one of the two dark suits
second meaning: the casino game also called twenty-one or pontoon

explanation.surface: A particular court card turns up in a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: In some rules this game is named after a winning hand holding a dark-suited jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a jack, and clubs and spades are the dark suits; the casino game twenty-one has the same name.

clue.text: Rod's backbone broken by dinner ladies initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words it follows
something broken by another is split open with it lodged inside

blocks.note: the spine is the backbone
the first letters of both words

explanation.surface: A man named Rod has his back hurt by school canteen staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Dinner ladies serve school lunches in Britain. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spindle is a slender rod on which thread is wound or around which something turns.

clue.text: Defective rim leaked, which is out of this world

indicators.note: defective means faulty or broken, so the letters are out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A faulty rim let something leak out, which is astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreamlike seems unreal, as if from a dream, and 'out of this world' means unearthly.

clue.text: Old cat with nine fractures

indicators.note: fractures break things apart, leaving the letters to be reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly cat has nine broken bones, one for each of its lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old, belonging to the distant past.

clue.text: Shoe helps athlete get prepare

blocks.note: first meaning: a soft sports shoe
second meaning: a coach who gets sportspeople ready

explanation.surface: A shoe that assists a runner in getting ready.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'prepare' where 'prepared' is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a sports shoe, and also a person who coaches athletes for competition.

clue.text: Assemble child's bed outside back room

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so the word is read from its end
outside means placed around, so the first word surrounds the second

blocks.note: a cot is a baby's bed
a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: Instructions to put together a crib outside a rear room of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back room' reads as one phrase; 'back' belongs to the reversal and 'room' is CELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect is to gather together, a synonym of assemble.

clue.text: Talk over each university in French castle

blocks.note: to chat is to talk
EA is the abbreviation for each
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Discussing each university while sitting in a castle in France.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first part above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or large country house.

clue.text: Greeting a thousand and one saints

blocks.note: K stands for a thousand, as in kilo
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the abbreviation for saint, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A welcome extended to a huge crowd of holy people.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss on the cheek is a common form of greeting someone.

clue.text: Round of applause for Sarah, getting very old

blocks.note: Sal is a pet name for Sarah
V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Sarah gets an ovation for reaching a great age.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a sudden burst of cheering, from its sense of guns fired together.

clue.text: Trooper's cry to chap to hold lava back

indicators.note: back means turned round, so this word runs from its end
to hold something is to keep it within, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A soldier shouts to a fellow to keep the molten rock at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a soldier in a cavalry or armoured unit, and a cavalryman fights on horseback.

clue.text: Observes uphill attack

indicators.note: in a down clue going uphill means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to set on someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A general watches an assault up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to observe or notice it, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Knock out, using bananas on the turn

indicators.note: on the turn means turning round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: bananas and nuts are both slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone is floored by fruit that is going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the turn' suggests fruit going bad, but it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to daze or render them unconscious, as a blow that knocks them out.

clue.text: Suddenly twirling this lance a lot!

indicators.note: twirling spins things round so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A knight abruptly spins his lance round and round, perhaps Sir Lancelot himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lance a lot' is a play on the name of the knight Lancelot.
explanation.definitionFit: All at once is an idiom meaning without warning, abruptly, the same as suddenly.

clue.text: Live for a second in retirement

indicators.note: in places one element inside the other

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
an exit is a departure or withdrawal

explanation.surface: Advice to enjoy a brief moment after retiring from work.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is a withdrawal or leaving, not stopping work.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being alive and having being are the same state, so the verb live can replace exist in a sentence.

clue.text: King today with name identified

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
now means at the present time
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A monarch is recognised by name in the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something known has been recognised or determined, a synonym for identified.

clue.text: Circular cape: squares don't have it

blocks.note: round means circular
a ness is a headland, a cape on the coast

explanation.surface: A circular cloak that squares avoid, as if fashion-conscious types shun it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squares' looks like slang for unfashionable people, but it means the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundness is the quality of being circular, which a square shape lacks.
